newsitem.title: ITALY: Israeli minister says peace process will continue.
newsitem.headline: Israeli minister says peace process will continue.

text.p: Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy said on Thursday that Israel would continue the Middle East peace process while making sure its own security was not threatened.

"The new government has decided on a policy to continue the peace process," said Levy, speaking a day after the first meeting between Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yassar Arafat.

"Of course, this will be based on a reality to fight terrorism to ensure (Israel's) security," he told a news conference in Rome after meeting his Italian counterpart Lamberto Dini at the start of a European tour.
"I would like to note that we have received agreement on this from the Palestinians and Arafat."
Levy was scheduled to leave Rome immediately after his meeting with Dini for Dublin. Ireland holds the rotating European Union presidency.
Arafat was also in Rome on Thursday to see Dini and other Italian officials but he and Levy were not meeting.

Levy, who had been pressing Netanyahu to meet Arafat face to face, said their meeting on Wednesday on the Israeli-Gazan border was "the green light to begin discussions of the mechanisms" of restarting stalled talks on extending Palestinian self-rule in the West Bank and Gaza.
"And I'm happy about that," he added.

Netanyahu had delayed meeting Arafat, citing security concerns on Hebron. But the Likud prime minister came under strong pressure from the United States, co-sponsor of Middle East peace efforts to meet the Palestinian leader.
"I think we have embarked on the right road to find peace," Levy said. "The road is long...and difficult, but when you make the effort you find solutions."
He said Israel was committed to providing economic help to Gaza and the West Bank.
"Israel is making many efforts in that area including creating tens of thousands of jobs for Palestinians," Levy said. "Israel will give its share to help ease the economic problems in this area."
He said Israel would also pursue other avenues in the overall Mideast peace effort, although noting that "there are still many dangers to the north of our country".
He said Israel would like to like to see Lebanon "return to a sovereign nation" and to open a dialogue with Syria.
"Unfortunately the Syrian position is a stubborn one. Hopefully if they see progress with the Palestinians they will see this is the right road," Levy said.
Dini, who attended the news conference with Levy, said the Israeli minister had stressed that Israel needed assurances that the security of its territory would not be threatened.
He said Italy viewed the Netanyahu-Arafat meeting with "relative optimism", adding that Netanyahu was "on the right track".
